prerequisites: The knowledge of at least one procedural-imperative programming language, such as C, Pascal, or others.

learning_outcomes.text: The student will have good knowledge and comprehension of the concepts concerning the object-oriented programming paradigm.

The student will be able to apply the object-oriented programming paradigm learned during the course to prototype and implement programs using the Python language. Furthermore, the student will be able to understand prototypes realized by a third party.

Thanks to the learned knowledge, the student will be able to evaluate the positive and negative aspects of a prototype or the Python implementation of a program utilizing the object-oriented programming paradigm.
The student will be able to converse with skilled interlocutors about this course's contents and transmit them to interlocutors who lack this knowledge.
The student will be able to quickly learn different object-oriented languages.

syllabus_topics: Introduction of the object-oriented programming paradigm: Definition of object, class, attribute, method. Base concepts: encapsulation, composition, inheritance. Techniques for schematizing objects: class diagrams drawn accordingly to the Unified Modelling Language (UML).
Overview of the Python language: Introduction to the language, data types, Boolean operators, conditional structures, cycles, functions, data structures.
Objects in Python: Creation of classes and object initialization.
Modules: Using pre-defined modules and organizing the code creating new modules.
Inheritance: Usage of single inheritance in Python. Advanced concepts: multiple inheritances, polymorphism.
Exception handling: Raising and handling exceptions. Defining new exceptions extending the exception class.
Python data structures: The features of the objects of type tuple, list, dictionary.
Input/output: The features of the file objects.
Strings and serialization: The features of the string objects, regular expressions, the serialization of objects using the pickle module.
Iterators: The features of the objects of type iterator.
Libraries for scientific visualization: The library matplotlib
The usage of databases: The usage of MySQL databases employing objects made available by MySQL Connector/Python

assessment_methods.method: Written exam consisting of theoretical questions
Written exam consisting of exercises solved using Python language

assessment_rules: The maximum final mark is 32. Honors will be achieved by obtaining a final mark equal to or higher than 32. If there are any doubts about the autonomy of the student during the exam, an integrative oral exam will be given, whose grade will substitute the one obtained with the written test. If the integrative oral exam is considered insufficient, the entire exam will be considered insufficient.
bibliography: D. Phillips, Python 3 Object-Oriented Programming: Build robust and maintainable software with object-oriented design patterns in Python 3.8, Packt, 2018 (III edition).
J. Krogh, MySQL Connector/Python Revealed: SQL and NoSQL Data Storage Using MySQL for Python Programmers, Apress, 2018.
